top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards targeted protein degradation as one coherent achievement: a heterobifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex whose cooperativity is measurable, structurally resolved and tunable, converting binding into removal. That is a game-changer principle independent of any one target or company, and it is reproduced across many labs and E3 ligases. The three names divide credit cleanly: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the concept in 2001, and Ciulli supplied the VHL ligand chemistry, ternary-complex structures and cooperativity framework that made it a rational design discipline. The cereblon glue strand (Handa, Ito) is a separate mechanism-of-action history and is honestly left outside a citation worded around induced proximity. The weakness is that no degrader is yet an approved drug, so I rest the case on the chemical principle, not on clinical outcome. P002 is second because it keeps the PROTAC origin and adds base editing, my first alternative, but it drops Ciulli, whose contribution I consider essential, and splits the prize into two parts. P003 is mature and cleanly attributed but extends the 2010 cross-coupling prize to a new bond class, a smaller step than a new modality. A prize is still preferable to no award.
